Hi Maya — great to meet you and the Novus team today. Below is a concise recap plus attached samples; I'll follow up with a proposed MLP for the deep dive.

Quick answers + attached artifacts (schema_examples.json):

1) SDK & auth
- Server-to-server: recommend API keys with short TTL rotated via your KMS (server side). We also support mTLS for Private deployments.
- Client-assisted UIs: use a proxy token flow (issue short-lived session tokens via your backend). We do not recommend embedding long-lived API keys in browser clients.
- Samples: Node (server) snippet and browser proxy example in schema_examples.json.

2) Routing & rollout
- Routing is policy driven. You can set per-request hints: {"preferred_region":"us-east1","latency_budget_ms":120} — the routing layer will attempt matching pools; fallback rules are defined at the model route.
- For cost vs latency you can set a cost_budget flag (e.g., max_cost_usd_per_1k_tokens) or choose explicit model_variant tags (e.g., "gptx-8bit-fast" vs "gptx-qa-quant") in the request.

3) Structured output & tool-calling streaming semantics
- Streaming semantics: by default we stream token deltas. For tool-calls we emit a single well-formed tool call event when the model completes the tool call JSON. We do not stream partial, malformed JSON tool arguments — the runtime will buffer until it can emit a syntactically valid JSON tool event.
- If you need low-latency partial tool arguments (e.g., progressive arguments for long-running retrievals), we can enable "partial_tool_streaming" on the route but it requires explicit client-side logic to stitch and validate.

4) Embeddings + reranker pattern
- Recommendation: ANN for recall (cheap) + rerank with a smaller causal or cross-encoder model for precision. For typical QPS (200 qps) we see cost parity doing ANN + small causal reranker vs an all-in-one reranker at query time. Example configs in schema_examples.json.

5) Request/response schema + tokenization
- Token accounting: our SDKs expose a token_estimate() helper. Tokenization is based on model tokenizer (BPE/subword) — payload size for prompt + response determines billing.
- max_tokens: server-side cap prevents runaway completions; you should set a response cap (we recommend 256–1024 depending on UI).
- stop sequences: enforced server-side; when streaming, stop tokens are honored and the stream ends at the last emitted token before stop. If you rely on stop for structured output, prefer explicit tool-calls or JSON schema enforcement to avoid partial streaming ambiguity.

Next steps: I've attached schema_examples.json that contains: sample chat request/streaming response, completions-only example, and an embedding+reranker config. Proposed deep dive slots: Tue 14 Feb 2028 at 09:00 / 11:00 ET — please confirm which works for you.

Jordan
